reason: The cited evidence directly supports the premises: E2 states ESD works under normal atmospheric conditions without heating or deformation; E3 describes RESD forming a local liquid reaction phase and the high cooling rates producing nanoscale structures with improved wear resistance; E4 confirms use of low-pulse energy (0.01–0.07 J) and mentions AlSi-type electrodes for comparison. However, E4 only mentions AlSi electrodes as a benchmark, not as a proven source of improved hardness/wear resistance, leaving that specific premise slightly overstated.
premises: ESD can improve surface quality of titanium alloys under normal atmospheric conditions without heating or deformation
RESD forms a local liquid reaction phase that mixes electrode and substrate components to synthesize new phases
Extremely high cooling rates (10^5–10^6 °C/s) in RESD enable formation of ultra-dispersed, amorphous, and nanoscale structures
Low-pulse energy (0.01–0.07 J) ESD equipment can produce smoother surfaces
Low-melting Al-Si electrodes can be used in RESD to form coatings with improved wear resistance
